comparison: Perfect agreement on crystal structure determination (C4-C5, C55-C62, C136-C141). Both evaluations recognize the crystallographic data as well-supported and a key contribution. OpenEval provides technical validation details (resolution, phasing methods), while peer reviewers acknowledge this as a solid structural advance with no concerns raised.

Complete agreement on homodimerization findings (C63-C73, C125). Both evaluations support the structural and biochemical characterization of the dimer interface. OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from multiple techniques (crystallography, SEC, DLS, mutagenesis), while peer reviewers explicitly highlight the novel dimerization interface as a key finding.

Strong agreement on arginine mutagenesis experiments (C83-C96, C118-C119). Both evaluations view the systematic mutagenesis as convincing evidence for the binding site. OpenEval emphasizes the dose-response relationship and R-to-K substitution data, while peer reviewers praise the mutagenesis strategy and conclusions without criticism.

Strong agreement on chimera experiments (C101-C107). Both evaluations recognize the SCARF1/SCARF2 chimera studies as particularly strong evidence. OpenEval notes the systematic domain swapping provides evidence for necessity and sufficiency of the 133-221aa region, while peer reviewers specifically highlight the gain-of-function results as especially convincing.

Partial overlap on sequence conservation (C108, C131-C132). OpenEval supports phylogenetic evidence for functional divergence between SCARF1 and SCARF2. Peer reviewers acknowledge the chimera work involving SCARF2 but focus more on functional gain-of-function rather than sequence conservation per se.

Agreement on modified LDL binding characterization (C74-C78). Both evaluations support the binding experiments using flow cytometry, ELISA, and microscopy. OpenEval emphasizes Ca2+-independence and pH stability data, while peer reviewers describe the work as straightforward and valid. Peer R3 also covers deletion mutagenesis (C79-C82) not included in OpenEval R3.

Agreement on deletion mutagenesis (C79-C82, C6). Both evaluations support the systematic deletion experiments identifying the 133-221aa region as necessary for binding. OpenEval notes the interpretation about conformational changes is speculative but reasonable, while peer reviewers accept the findings as part of the overall convincing experimental approach.

Both address oligomerization state experiments (C97-C99). OpenEval rates these claims as UNCERTAIN due to contradictory ELISA vs flow cytometry results and speculative interpretations. Peer reviewers do not specifically critique these experiments, implicitly accepting them as part of the convincing overall approach, though they also consider pH experiments (C100) not in OpenEval R6.

Agreement on teichoic acid inhibition experiments (C8-C9, C109-C111, C128-C130). OpenEval supports the evidence for overlapping binding sites but notes the 'general binding position' conclusion is speculative. Peer reviewers do not specifically discuss these experiments but implicitly accept them as part of the straightforward experimental set without raising concerns.

Minimal overlap on Ca2+-independence (C78). OpenEval R10 specifically addresses Ca2+-binding mechanism (C115-C117) with structural and functional evidence. Peer R3 covers broader binding characterization including Ca2+-independence but does not specifically evaluate the mechanistic claims about absence of Ca2+-binding motifs.

Minimal overlap on mechanistic comparisons (C128). OpenEval R11 addresses literature comparisons to LOX-1, CD36, WIF-1, and SR-A family (C120-C124, C128), rating them as supported. Peer R6 implicitly accepts these as part of the overall experimental framework without specific evaluation.

OpenEval rates functional significance of dimerization for lipoprotein binding (C126-C127) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation and contradictory data. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers accept the dimerization structural findings (R2) without addressing functional implications for binding.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background claims (C1-C54, C113-C114, C133-C135, C142) as appropriately supported by literature citations. Peer reviewers do not specifically evaluate background/contextual claims, focusing instead on novel experimental findings.

OpenEval supports claim about curved conformation (C112) based on crystal structures and AlphaFold comparison. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers accept overall structural findings without specifically addressing AlphaFold comparisons.

Peer reviewers identify a key limitation: the work does not explain structural basis for binding specificity (why SCARF1 binds oxLDL/AcLDL but not LDL/HDL) despite identifying the binding site (C6-C7, C9). This represents an UNCERTAIN evaluation of mechanistic understanding. OpenEval addresses these claims in multiple results (R4, R5, R9) but rates them as SUPPORTED, not highlighting the specificity gap as prominently.
